cards.text: Years ago Jacob ran for his life, because his brother Esau planned to kill him. Now Jacob has sent droves of livestock on ahead as a gift for Esau. Then Jacob looks up and sees Esau coming toward him, and I bet his heart is pounding right out of his chest, because Esau is not coming alone.

cards.question: Jacob looks up and sees Esau coming toward him. How many men does Esau have with him?

cards.text: Four hundred men. FOUR. HUNDRED. So Jacob divides the children among his wives, Leah and Rachel, and the two maidservants.

cards.question: Jacob lines up his family to meet Esau. He puts ___ and Joseph at the rear.

cards.text: Maidservants and their children up front, Leah and her children next, Rachel and her son Joseph in the back. Then Jacob himself walks out ahead of all of them.

cards.question: As Jacob gets close to his brother Esau, he bows to the ground ___ times.
Jacob is bowing low as Esau and his four hundred men get close. What does Esau do?

answers.text: He orders his men to surround Jacob
He stops and waits in silence

cards.text: Esau runs to him, throws his arms around his neck and kisses him, and they both weep. Four hundred men standing right there, and I bet every one of them suddenly found the ground REAL interesting.

cards.question: Esau looks up, sees the women and children, and asks who they are. How does Jacob describe the children?

answers.text: God graciously gave them to him
They will carry on the family name
They are his reward for hard work

cards.text: Then the family comes forward, group by group. The maidservants and their children, then Leah and hers, then Joseph and Rachel, and every one of them bows down.

cards.question: Esau asks Jacob what he means by sending this whole company of livestock out to meet him. What does Jacob say?

answers.text: To find favor in your sight
To repay the debt I owe you
To show the riches in my hand

cards.question: Jacob offers Esau the droves of livestock as a gift. Esau accepts them as soon as Jacob offers.

cards.text: Esau says he already has plenty and tells his brother to keep what belongs to him. But Jacob insists, "No, please!"
Jacob tells Esau, "I have seen your face, and it is like seeing the face of God…" Nobody has EVER said that about my face, friend.

cards.question: Jacob says seeing Esau's face is like seeing the face of God because Esau has received him favorably.

cards.text: Jacob says God has been gracious to him and he has all he needs. So one brother has plenty, the other has all he needs, and they're arguing over who has to keep the gift.

cards.question: Jacob keeps pressing Esau until Esau accepts the gift.

cards.text: Gift settled. Esau says, "Let us be on our way, and I will go ahead of you."

cards.question: Esau wants them to travel together with him leading the way. What reason does Jacob give for holding back?

answers.text: His children are frail and his herds are nursing
His servants are worn out from the long trip
His wives need to rest for a few days first

cards.text: Jacob says if they're driven hard for even a day, all the animals will die. Same with my dough, friend: rush it and the whole batch comes out flat.

cards.question: Jacob asks Esau to go on ahead and says he'll follow slowly, at a pace the livestock and children can handle, until he comes to him at ___.

cards.text: Esau tries one more thing. He offers to leave some of his people with Jacob, like a free escort.

cards.question: Jacob gladly takes Esau up on his offer to leave some of his people with him.

cards.text: Jacob says, "Why do that? Let me find favor in the sight of my lord." So that day Esau starts on his way back to Seir.

cards.question: After Esau heads back to Seir, Jacob follows him there.

cards.text: Instead, Jacob builds a house for himself and shelters for his livestock. I spent years in a junk drawer, so trust me, I respect a man who finally gets his own space.

cards.question: Because of the shelters Jacob builds for his livestock there, the place is called ___.

cards.text: After coming from Paddan-aram, Jacob arrives safely at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan and camps just outside the city. Seven bows and four hundred men later, safely sounds REAL good.

cards.question: Jacob pitches his tent just outside the city of Shechem, on ground that belongs to the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father. How does Jacob get that plot of ground?

answers.text: They give it to him freely
He takes it from them by force

cards.question: Jacob pays the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father, a hundred pieces of silver for his plot. What does he set up on it?

cards.text: He calls the altar El-Elohe-Israel. Stay close, friend, because Jacob's family still has plenty of road ahead of them.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from outside the passage without their references. Jacob fleeing because Esau planned to kill him comes from Genesis 27:41-43, and the droves sent ahead as a gift come from Genesis 32:13-21. The card cites only Genesis 33:1.

rule.text: Every fact and every verse number comes from that text. Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The outside facts on this card (Gen 27:41-43, Gen 32:13-21) carry no reference.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Joseph first appears here as part of the blank question, with no word on who he is. He is only called Rachel's son on card 5, after the question.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 4 just told the baker that Jacob promised to follow Esau slowly until he came to him at Seir. A thoughtful baker reasoning from the earlier cards would pick True, so the right answer (False, Jacob goes to Succoth) is a trap rather than an informed guess. The cards before it need more context, or the question needs to ask something different.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
